source.title: Inter-layer Collision Networks
source.authors: Jun-Yi An; Fengshan Liu; Fu-Rao Shen; Jian Zhao

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports training curves and explicit training-error outcomes for modified and baseline CNNs, bearing on whether gradient-trained networks attain low training error. It does not test the general claim across CIFAR-10/100, random labels, or the listed training conditions.
record.gate_note: Rows cover reported training-error curves and statements about training accuracy for the paper's own ImageNet and CIFAR-10 experiments. Test-error-only comparisons and cited prior work are not rows. Curve values not stated numerically in text are recorded as figure only.
record.test_reason: The study reports approximately 100% training accuracy for two IC convolutional networks trained with SGD on CIFAR-10, directly bearing on V1 in a new architecture setting. It does not experimentally isolate width, identity shortcuts, initialization, stability thresholds, or batch normalization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: IC structures improve convergence speed and usually improve classification accuracy, with additional computation. The authors also report exceptions: IC-SE-ResNet-50 and IC-ResNeXt have slightly worse test accuracy despite approximately 100% training accuracy, and IC bottleneck blocks increase overfitting risk.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains modified IC CNN architectures and baseline networks for image classification; it does not reproduce the claim's broad benchmark or corrupted-label recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture and IC unit type change convergence and generalization outcomes; the paper reports overfitting for IC-ResNet-50, IC-ResNeXt and IC-SE-ResNet-50.

fits_no_version.finding: IC structures improve convergence speed relative to baseline architectures on ImageNet and CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding IC layers or blocks can accelerate CNN optimization under the tested training recipes.

record.problems: No training-error numbers are stated for most models; their values are only shown in plots. Only two modified CIFAR10 models receive an explicit near-100% training-accuracy statement. Experiments are on ImageNet and CIFAR10, not CIFAR100 or corrupted labels.
record.rows_left_out: No separately stated test-error-only values were included. Figure 4(e) for IC-SE-ResNet-50 and baseline SE-ResNet-50 is not a separate row because the text provides an explicit training-accuracy result for the IC model and does not state a numeric baseline train error; the plotted curves are covered only where separately identified in R13–R16. ImageNet table values are validation error, not training error.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, Adam, explicit random-initialization conditions, and controlled comparisons involving model size, early stopping, or regularized recipes leaving substantial training error.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization, spurious local minima, and the effect of adding student neurons.
Depth-induced training degradation in plain networks and its prevention by identity shortcuts; special initialization and normalization-free residual training.
Initialization comparisons, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, curvature dynamics, recovery, and divergence.
Controlled normalization comparisons, higher-learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training.

record.verdict_notes: Unreadable curve endpoints do not justify limits_scope verdicts. R15 incorrectly extends a statement about two IC models to a baseline model. The ImageNet comparisons, including the additional ResNet-101 experiment, do not test V1's specified CIFAR setting; their generalization gaps also do not test the mechanisms named by V2–V6. This study is not an original source for any supplied version.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, small models as a size comparison, early stopping, Adam, and substantial-error outcomes for smaller models or regularized recipes are not tested.
